Use closure of \(C^n\) maps under composition. Since \(\sinh:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\) is \(C^\infty\), composing it with the assumed \(C^n\) map \(f\) shows that \(x\mapsto\sinh(f(x))\) is \(C^n\) on \(s\).

For the equivalence, prove both sides independently from the exponential representations of the hyperbolic functions:

- \((\sinh)'=\cosh\) on \(\mathbb R\), strengthened to a strict derivative;
- \((\cosh)'=\sinh\) on \(\mathbb C\).

Both universally quantified propositions are therefore true, so their equivalence follows immediately. The key assumption is the global \(C^\infty\) regularity of \(\sinh\), which handles arbitrary \(n:\mathrm{WithTop}\,\mathrm{ENat}\).
